title: Idris Elba and King Charles III Explore Five Decades of The King's Trust in New Netflix Documentary
excerpt:
Netflix's The Trust follows Idris Elba as he examines the charity that helped him early in his acting career.
The documentary arrives on December 26, 2026, marking the organization's 50th anniversary.
body_md:
Idris Elba is bringing a deeply personal perspective to a new Netflix documentary about the charity founded by King Charles III. Titled The Trust, the film examines how access to practical support, training and opportunity can alter the course of a young person's life. The project arrives as The King's Trust marks 50 years since Charles established the organization in 1976, when he was still Prince of Wales.

The connection is not simply that Elba is a famous supporter. Growing up in East London, the future Luther star received a grant from the organization that helped him pursue acting. In the documentary's trailer, he reflects on how differently his life might have unfolded without that intervention. His own career provides an entry point into a broader story about young people navigating barriers to education, employment and professional confidence.

Filmed over the course of a year, the documentary explores the work of an organization that says it has helped more than 1.5 million young people worldwide develop skills and confidence for employment. Rather than focusing exclusively on a celebrity biography, the film aims to illuminate the practical consequences of being offered an opportunity at a crucial moment. Elba's story gives those larger statistics a recognizable human dimension.

King Charles III also appears in the documentary, which considers the relationship between the monarch and the actor and the shared interest in the charity's mission that brought them together. Their contrasting backgrounds offer a distinctive framework for exploring the Trust's history. This is not presented as a conventional behind-the-scenes portrait of the royal family; the organization's work and the young people it supports remain central to the premise.

The documentary is produced by Elba's independent company 22 Summers, which he runs with Diene Petterle and Gina Carter. Ashley Francis-Roy directs, Clare Bradbury serves as showrunner, and Petterle, Eva Omaghomi and Jonathan Smith are executive producers. Netflix has scheduled the release for Boxing Day, December 26, 2026, tying the film's arrival to the organization's anniversary year.

The Trust was originally known as the Prince's Trust and has attracted high-profile supporters over the decades, including Benedict Cumberbatch, Gemma Arterton and Gary Lineker. Their history as supporters should not be confused with confirmed appearances in the documentary: the initial announcement does not establish that they are interview subjects. Likewise, the publicly available description does not provide a complete list of contributors or a detailed scene-by-scene account of the finished film.

For viewers interested in social-impact documentaries, the project offers a chance to see a less familiar aspect of Elba's story: not only what he achieved, but one of the early opportunities that helped make those achievements possible. The documentary's ultimate effectiveness will depend on how fully it represents the experiences of young people beyond its famous participants. For now, the confirmed details are its subject, principal creative team and Netflix release date.
